history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Built in 1848 by Sheth Hutheesing Kesarisinh, a wealthy Ahmedabad Jain merchant; after his death at age 49, his wife Shethani Harkunwar supervised completion (early 1850s). A white-marble Maru-Gurjara (Solanki) temple dedicated to Dharmanatha, the 15th Tirthankara, in the Shvetambara tradition, blended with haveli elements. Chief architect Premchand Salat; the ~Rs 10 lakh cost employed hundreds of artisans for two years during a severe Gujarat famine. The complex holds a 52.5-metre-tall main shrine, 52 devakulika shrines, and a 78-ft free-standing Manastambha pillar. It is managed by the Hutheesing family trust.

name: Hutheesing Jain Temple
town_description: Ahmedabad is Gujarat's largest city and its former capital, founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmed Shah I on the banks of the Sabarmati river. Its walled old city became India's first UNESCO World Heritage City in 2017, known for carved wooden havelis, pols, stepwells, and Sultanate-era monuments. Today it is a major industrial and commercial hub, famous for its food culture, the Sabarmati Ashram, and as the gateway to Gujarat.
